open_webui.title: Open WebUI
open_webui.help: To chat with an Open WebUI model from the Assistant page, without going through Home Assistant.
open_webui.invalid: Invalid address: it starts with http:// or https://.
open_webui.tools: Give WattSlot's data to Open WebUI
open_webui.tools_server: In Open WebUI: Admin Panel › Settings › External Tools › “+”, type MCP (Streamable HTTP), with the app's MCP server address above.
open_webui.tools_model: Then Workspace › Models › edit the chosen model › Tools: tick the WattSlot server. Also paste the recommended prompt (Assistant page) into its system prompt if you want it by default.
open_webui.tools_addon: As an add-on, the MCP server can only be reached by Home Assistant: an Open WebUI installed elsewhere cannot use it. The model then answers without WattSlot's data.
open_webui.tools_standalone: Open WebUI must be able to reach the app's address on your local network.

objective.title: Planning objective

presets.autonomy: autonomy (buying the least from the grid)
presets.self_consumption: self-consumption (sending the least surplus to the grid)

hints.cost: Lowest bill: buy at the cheapest hours, use the surplus rather than selling it at a low price.
hints.autonomy: The least energy taken from the grid, even if it is a bit more expensive.
hints.self_consumption: Use as much of the production on site as possible, even if it means buying at peak hours.
hints.co2: Buy at the hours when grid electricity emits the least CO₂.
hints.custom: Compromise between the criteria, according to the weights below.

objective.weights_hint: In euro equivalent: a kWh bought from or sent to the grid is worth the average price of the day. Only the ratio between weights matters.
objective.co2_entity: Grid carbon intensity (Home Assistant sensor, g/kWh)
objective.co2_hint: Its forecast if it gives one, otherwise its current value for the whole day: the plan is then the autonomy one, with CO₂ as an indicator.

grid_import.definition: The electricity the home takes from the grid when the sun and the battery are not enough.

surplus.definition: The solar production the home does not use and the battery cannot store.

self_consumption.definition: The share of your solar production used on site.

autonomy.definition: The share of your consumption covered without buying from the grid.

off_peak.definition: The hours when your contract charges less per kWh.

kwh.definition: The kWh measures energy (what you pay for); the kW measures power (energy per hour).

kwp.definition: The power of solar panels in full sun, given by the installer.

cycle.definition: An appliance program (washing, drying…) that runs for a while once started.

floor.definition: The charge level below which the battery does not go.

energy_dashboard.definition: The Home Assistant page where your panels, meter and measured appliances are declared.

sensor.definition: A Home Assistant measurement (energy, power, charge level) linked to a device.

assistant.title: Voice assistant
assistant.intro: Ask Home Assistant's Assist about your energy, with the language model you already have (Ollama on your network, or an online service). The plan is still computed by the application; the assistant reads and explains it.

step1.title: 1. Connect the application in Home Assistant
step1.help: In Home Assistant: Settings › Devices & services › Add integration › “Model Context Protocol”, with this address:
step1.addon: Address on Home Assistant's internal network: only Home Assistant can reach it.
step1.standalone: Address of the application on your local network: Home Assistant must be able to reach it. The application has no login of its own: do not expose it to the Internet.

step2.title: 2. Choose the conversation agent
step2.agent: Add a conversation agent: the Ollama integration (model on your network) or an online service's integration.
step2.model: Choose a model that can call tools, with a context size of at least 8,192 tokens.
step2.api: In the agent's options, choose the application's MCP server as the LLM API, then pick this agent in Assist.

step3.title: 3. Paste the advised prompt
step3.help: Paste this text into the conversation agent's instructions: it tells it which tool to use and not to invent anything.
